title: Anjali Sud to Lead SiriusXM as CEO From January 2027
headline: Anjali Sud to Lead SiriusXM as CEO From January 2027
subheadline: The Indian-origin executive who scaled Tubi past 110 million monthly users will succeed Jennifer Witz at the largest US satellite radio company.
summary: The Indian-origin executive who scaled Tubi past 110 million monthly users will succeed Jennifer Witz at the largest US satellite radio company.
excerpt: The Indian-origin executive who scaled Tubi past 110 million monthly users will succeed Jennifer Witz at the largest US satellite radio company.
body:
• SiriusXM has appointed Anjali Sud as its next chief executive, effective January 1, 2027.
  • Sud, an Indian-origin media executive, currently leads Fox's streaming service Tubi, which she grew to more than 110 million monthly active users.
  • She succeeds Jennifer Witz, who steps down after almost 25 years at SiriusXM, including nearly six as CEO, and stays on as an adviser through the end of 2027.
  • Before Tubi, Sud was CEO of Vimeo, where she took the company public and built it into a profitable platform with 300 million users.

SiriusXM, the largest satellite radio company in the United States, has turned to a streaming executive to lead its next phase. The company announced on Monday, November 9, 2026, that Anjali Sud will become chief executive on January 1, 2027, succeeding Jennifer Witz. According to Reuters, the appointment turns to a digital media veteran to help reinvigorate growth as listeners shift away from satellite radio.

The appointment

Sud has been an independent director on SiriusXM's board since March 2025 and will remain a board member after she takes over, the company said in its announcement. Witz is stepping down after almost two and a half decades at the company, including nearly six years as CEO, and will remain in an advisory role until the end of 2027.

"I am honored to lead SiriusXM in its next chapter. Premium audio experiences will be more important than ever to the future of entertainment, and I believe SiriusXM can evolve to lead that future."

— Anjali Sud

Board chairman Greg Maffei said Sud "has built some of the most successful consumer entertainment platforms," scaling audiences across businesses supported by both advertising and subscription models, and that her time on the board gives her direct knowledge of the company's strategy.

The record she brings

Sud has led Tubi, Fox Corporation's free streaming service, since 2023. Under her leadership the service grew to more than 110 million monthly active users, expanded globally and drove profitable growth, according to SiriusXM. Before Tubi, she served as chief executive of Vimeo, where she took the company public and led its transformation into a profitable, global video platform with 300 million users. Earlier in her career she held roles in e-commerce, finance and media at Amazon and Time Warner. She holds an undergraduate degree from the Wharton School at the University of Pennsylvania and an MBA from Harvard Business School, and also serves on the boards of Dolby Laboratories and Change.org.

What she inherits

SiriusXM reaches approximately 255 million monthly listeners across its subscription service, Pandora, its podcast network and its advertising businesses, the company says. It has struggled to chart its future as more listeners choose streaming: Reuters reported third-quarter revenue of $2.15 billion, slightly below the $2.16 billion analysts had expected, according to data compiled by LSEG. Maffei credited Witz with returning the company to revenue growth and generating near-record levels of free cash flow, along with record-high customer satisfaction and record-low churn. Sud's task, starting in January, is to convert the company's streaming and podcast assets into growth without giving up the economics of the satellite business that still funds them.
